notes: Java (lines 160-165): reads server.properties['level-name'], trims it, and falls back to the literal string "world" when the key is absent or blank after trimming -- case 1. A present, non-blank value is trimmed and returned as-is -- case 2 shows trailing whitespace stripped. Bedrock (lines 156-159): reads BedrockPropertiesManager's levelName, trims it, and falls back to "Bedrock level" when blank -- case 3. A non-blank value passes through trimmed -- case 4. The two server types use different fallback strings on purpose ("world" matches vanilla/Paper's own default level-name; "Bedrock level" matches BDS's own default), so a Rust port must not unify them into one shared constant.
